**Key visual observations:**
- Stem base at soil line, plant pulled from ground showing the crown/root area
- Stem has been **cut longitudinally**, exposing internal pith tissue — visible bleached, white/tan internal tissue
- **White fungal material** visible on the outside of the stem at the soil line
- Entire plant is dead: leaves are brown, wilted, and desiccated
- Stem appears girdled at the soil line

**Reasoning through candidates:**

- **Sclerotinia_Timber_Rot**: "Water-soaked areas develop on the stem that become covered with white cotton-like mycelium, bleached and hardened... positive identification achieved by slicing the diseased stem longitudinally." The longitudinal cut of the stem showing bleached internal tissue is a direct match to this diagnostic criterion. Sclerotia (rice-grain-sized, black) would be embedded inside.

- **Southern_Blight**: Features white cottony mycelium at the stem base and small mustard-seed sclerotia radiating onto the soil surface. The mycelium would appear more prominently spreading outward onto the surrounding soil.

The **longitudinal stem cut** is the defining diagnostic feature here, combined with the bleached internal stem tissue and white mycelium — both hallmarks of Sclerotinia Timber Rot. Southern Blight sclerotia would appear as small spherical bodies on the soil surface, which are not prominently visible here.
